sources.citation: Böhtlingk, Otto von. 1851. Über die Sprache der Jakuten, Jakutische Grammatik, §128 'Betonung', p. 151 — read via archive.org scan rosettaproject_sah_morsyn-1 (scanned text; page confirmed by running heads 'Jakutische Grammatik. 151' / '152 Ueber die Sprache der Jakuten'). Also read: Stanford Phonology…
sources.quote: Böhtlingk: "In Yakut the accent rests, as far as I have been able to observe, always on the final syllable of the word." (He adds that Middendorff found the same, and that Ogorodnikov's 'mostly on the last syllable' reflects confusing vowel length with accent.)

sources.citation: Normanskaja, Julia V. & Legusina, Ulyana N. 2022. Dolgie glasnye v jakutskix knigax serediny XIX v.: oshibki ili otrazhenie tonkix prosodicheskix protivopostavlenij...? Oriental Studies 15(1): 132-143. DOI 10.22162/2619-0990-2022-59-1-132-143 (open access, cyberleninka).
sources.quote: Russian abstract: 'glasnyj pervogo sloga vydelen po dolgote i intensivnosti po sravneniju s glasnym vtorogo sloga, na kotoryj obychno padaet udarenie v literaturnom jakutskom jazyke'; English abstract p.133: '...as compared to vowel sounds in the second one usually stressed in standard Yakut. This emphasis is as sporadic...'. Praat measurements (Vilyuysk, Verkhoyansk dialects) show sporadic extra duration/intensity on the FIRST syllable of inflected monosyllabic stems, described as a previously undescribed dialectal prosodic feature needing further study.
sources.locator: abstract pp.132-133 (Russian) and p.133 (English); results table and conclusion p.141
